tob-10554: James Legge’s classic translation of the Tao Te Ching presents all eighty-one chapters of Lao Tzu’s enigmatic masterpiece. Its brief verses urge rulers to govern lightly, praise the strength found in softness, and point to the Tao — the unnameable source of all things. As one of the earliest English versions, Legge’s rendering introduced generations of Western readers to Chinese philosophy.
tob-13554: Drawn from al-Ghazali’s vast Ihya — his ‘Revival of the Religious Sciences’ — these extracts present his teachings on worship, character, and the purification of the heart. They show the great theologian at his most practical, guiding ordinary believers toward sincerity and self-knowledge. The selection offers the essence of medieval Islam’s most influential moralist.
tob-4054: The first volume of Blavatsky’s Secret Doctrine, called Cosmogenesis, unrolls her vast story of how the world began — rounds of making and unmaking over ages, steered by unseen minds. Built on Hindu lore and her own claimed visions, it is the most daring world-picture in all of occult writing.
tob-4254: Her-Ra-Ma-ëL’s 1918 French study of Voodoo’s fiends tracks Haiti’s ghosts — their names, rites, and powers. The work is one early European’s chart of the living faith. Its wonder-seeking eye tints the tale. A strange keepsake of young Vodou book-lore.
copyright-renewals-1954: This official Library of Congress volume lists every copyright renewal registered in the United States during 1954. Authors, publishers, and lawyers used such catalogs to track who still held rights in books, music, films, and plays. Today the volume serves researchers and rights-holders as a historical record of American creative ownership in the mid-twentieth century.
personal-narrative-of-travels-to-the-equ: Another volume of Humboldt's immortal travel narrative, carrying his South American explorations ever deeper into the unknown. Volcanoes climbed, rivers mapped, and nature studied with tireless zeal fill these pages. The great naturalist's masterpiece rolls on. Jungles, savannas, and Andean heights pass before his ever-curious eyes.
arxiv-2605-08854: Blurry photos hide the sharp image underneath, and blind deblurring must recover it without knowing how the blur happened. Insoo Kim and Jinwoo Shin align generative flow models with the restoration goal, steering the generation toward the true sharp image. The 2026 paper brings modern generative modeling to the classic problem of motion blur.
arxiv-2605-09054: Data streams never end, and privacy must hold for every window of events — w-event privacy — while letting each user set their own bar. Leilei Du, Xu Zhou, Peng Cheng, and colleagues design personalized privacy for infinite stream estimation. The 2026 paper is differential privacy that respects individual preferences.
arxiv-2605-09354: A single operator has a spectral radius that governs its long-term behavior; a tuple of operators needs a subtler joint notion. Marcel Scherer, Orr Moshe Shalit, and Eli Shamovich investigate the spectral radius of operator tuples. The 2026 paper is operator theory on joint spectra and their mysteries.
arxiv-2605-09454: Single-index bandits model decisions driven by one hidden direction in a high-dimensional world — a realistic middle ground. Devdan Dey, Sujoy Bhore, and Avishek Ghosh nail down the optimal regret for the setting. The 2026 paper is bandit theory with the best possible guarantees.
arxiv-2605-09654: Diffusion models sample beautifully but lack the ironclad guarantees of MCMC; Metropolis adjustment could supply them. Kevin H. Lam, Tyler Farghly, Christopher Williams, and Jun Yang build Metropolis-adjusted diffusion models. The 2026 paper marries generative AI with classical sampling theory.
arxiv-2605-10354: Initial conditions for stereographic cosmological simulations — stepsic generates them. Balázs Pál, Gábor Rácz, István Csabai, and István Szapudi build the generator. The 2026 paper is cosmology software. It generates the right initial conditions for stereographic cosmological simulations.
arxiv-2605-10454: A flexible Raspberry Pi-based data logger platform for Modbus sensors, deployed with Ansible. This 2026 paper presents the open platform. It is IoT engineering for industry. It flexibly logs Modbus sensor data on Raspberry Pi hardware. Modbus sensors logged reliably.
pmc-13458354: Artificial intelligence in spiritual care — explored through a modified Delphi study of experts. Fabian Winiger, C Estelle Smith, Shadi Nourriz, and colleagues convene the panel. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is digital chaplaincy. It asks experts what AI means for the soul.
pmc-13402254: The Toumai robotic surgical system in general surgery — early clinical experience systematically reviewed. pmc-13418854: Marginal zone lymphoma treated with bispecific antibodies — follicular lymphoma emerging afterward, unmasking a composite lymphoma. pmc-13521154: Post-traumatic hemorrhagic synovitis of the shoulder — reported as a case. Jinxin Zhang, Chengjun Hao, Houzhi Huang, and colleagues describe the presentation. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is shoulder pathology. It documents blood in the joint after trauma. Synovitis, post-traumatic.
pmc-13467054: Bethesda III to IV thyroid nodules — the diagnostic accuracy of combined fine-needle aspiration biopsy and ultrasonography for malignancy. pmc-13426354: Discogenic low back pain — core acupoints and acupoint combination patterns for acupuncture, found by data mining. Yiqi Dong, Yunyun Xu, Shuwen Wu, and colleagues mine the data. The 2026 Europe PMC paper is acupuncture. It data-mines the best needle points for backs.
arxiv-2606-17054: Kevin Yuanbo Wu and colleagues tackle universal grasping, the dream of a robot hand that can pick up anything a person can. arxiv-2606-17154: Stephen Powell derives the height field theory for the two-dimensional classical dimer model, where dominoes tile a grid, starting from a Grassmann representation. arxiv-2606-17254: Girish and colleagues detect Alzheimer's across languages without retraining for each tongue. arxiv-2606-17354: Jacob Bremerman and colleagues build an operationalizable ontology for untranslatability, the words and concepts that resist translation. arxiv-2606-17454: Gaurav Gupta and colleagues dissect model behavior through agent trajectories. Instead of probing a model with single questions, they watch what it does across whole tasks. The trajectory reveals habits and failure modes invisible to static tests, a new lens on AI behavior.
arxiv-2606-17554: Soham Dutta and Arnab Saha study the Brownian gyration of an inertial ellipsoid. The lopsided particle tumbles under thermal kicks, and inertia adds memory to the dance. arxiv-2606-17854: Deepak Ajwani and colleagues refute Wegner's conjecture for axis-parallel rectangles with a counterexample. The conjecture bounded how many colors rectangle contact graphs need. arxiv-2606-18054: Lingfeng and colleagues extract AI-based cognitive-linguistic features for dementia assessment from picture description. arxiv-2606-18154: Ziqi Zhou and colleagues learn cardiac electrophysiology digital twins through agentic discovery of hybrid structures. arxiv-2606-18454: Pratik Deshmukh and colleagues verify neural networks with attack guidance and dataset-dependent training in Veriphi. The verifier learns from attacks where to look hardest. plos-pone-0003454: Immunologists found HIV-fighting cells gathering in the wrong place in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003554: Eye researchers found a famous growth factor moonlighting as a lifeguard in this 2008 paper. plos-pone-0003654: In 2008, Serrano and De Los Rios studied how flow systems stay efficient. plos-pone-0003754: In 2008, Ulrich Kirk scanned brains judging beauty in context. The same object pleased more or less depending on its setting, and brain imaging revealed where context bends aesthetic judgment. The study shows taste is not just in the object but in the frame around it.
plos-pone-0003854: Working in 2008, a team purified a gizzard protein and probed its chemistry. Gastrokine-1, isolated from chicken gizzard smooth muscle, was characterized for its biochemical properties. The groundwork sets up future study of what this muscle protein actually does.
plos-pone-0003954: In 2008, Derikx, van Waardenburg, and Thuijls found surgery breaching the gut wall. Major non-abdominal operations still caused loss of intestinal barrier function in patients. The finding implicates gut leakage in complications far from the surgical site.

plos-pone-0004154: In 2009, Lane Yoder mapped brain states with plain logic. Explicit logic circuits distinguished rival neural states. plos-pone-0004454: In 2009, Ermakova, Shnol, and Panteleev modeled waves in flowing matter. Excitation waves in moving media were studied via the FitzHugh-Nagumo model. The flows bent the wave fronts sharply. The math serves blood-clotting and bioreactor models well. The work is purely theoretical.
plos-pone-0004554: In 2009, He, Wang, and Li built a clever protein-interaction text miner. PPI Finder mined human protein-protein interactions from the literature. The handy tool tamed the swelling publication flood. The method aids network biology research. The neat mining is text-based and fast.
plos-pone-0004654: In 2009, Pistis, Piras, and Pirastu found eight villages worlds apart by genes. Eight cut-off Sardinian villages showed big gene differences. The cut-off life molded distinct gene pools over time. The study helps future gene-link studies. The area is cut off still.
plos-pone-0004754: In 2009, Wiedemann, Loell, and Mueller found stomach-bug toxins sparking later trouble anew. plos-pone-0338854: When the muscles that lift the eye swell, vision can double or the eye can bulge — and the cause is often unclear. plos-pone-0358654: A lab artifact was quietly corrupting experiments: ambient light was driving verteporfin-induced protein cross-linking during routine sample processing. plos-pone-0357054: From Bronze Age huts to Iron Age towns, Latium vetus transformed — and AI can help explain how. plos-pone-0358454: A coral colony isn’t uniform — different spots do different jobs. plos-pone-0358254: Wet rock breaks differently from dry rock — a fact tunnels and dams ignore at their peril. plos-pone-0357754: Hepatitis B mutates to escape control — especially in its precore and basal core promoter regions. plos-pone-0354154: Saudi Arabia’s cities are sprawling at breakneck speed. plos-pone-0354954: Cultural values profoundly shape Mexican American college students’ lives — and researchers need valid tools to study them. plos-pone-0354454: Russian knapweed — Acroptilon repens — wages chemical warfare on neighboring plants. The plant’s own herbicide could become agriculture’s.
plos-pone-0345554: What you see and hear while running changes how tired you get. This paper tested the effects of visual pacing cues and motivational auditory content on running fatigue and biomechanics. The findings give coaches and app designers evidence-based tools to keep runners going stronger, longer.
plos-pone-0355554: A dog’s whiskers are precision instruments — and their follicles are engineering marvels. This paper provided histomorphological and ultrastructural analysis of the vibrissal follicle-sinus complexes in dogs. The microscopic anatomy explains how whiskers transduce the faintest touch into neural signals.
plos-pone-0356254: Saudi educators under Vision 2030’s sweeping reforms face moral injury alongside burnout. This interpretative phenomenological study explored their systemic ethical tensions. The lived accounts reveal professionals caught between conscience and compliance — essential reading for reformers who forget the human cost of transformation.
plos-pone-0355354: ICU directors’ ability to practice protective ventilation depends on what resources they have. This nationwide cross-sectional study associated resource availability with knowledge, attitudes, and practice of protective ventilation. The findings expose how equipment gaps — not just knowledge gaps — endanger ventilated patients.
plos-pone-0345854: Ranking anticancer drugs by neural networks is powerful — but opaque models don’t earn oncologists’ trust. This paper shed light on neural learning-to-rank models for anticancer drug prioritization. The interpretability work reveals what the models actually learn — the first step toward clinical adoption.
plos-pone-0355854: Epilepsy’s treatment gap in Ghana — people needing care but not getting it — was unmeasured. This paper quantified the barriers to epilepsy care in rural and peri-urban districts. The measured gap demands action: anti-seizure medications exist, but too many Ghanaians still suffer without them.
plos-pone-0353754: Who we want to spend time with depends on our temperament meeting the moment’s motivations. This paper showed that state and perceived partner motivations interact with approach-avoidance temperament to predict social preferences in daily life. The findings map the hidden psychology of everyday affiliation — why we approach some people and avoid others.
plos-pone-0355054: Dendritic cells — the immune system’s sentinels — need Tyro3 to properly present antigens. The findings reveal a molecular gatekeeper of immune surveillance — with implications for vaccines and cancer immunotherapy.
plos-pone-0354354: Prostate cancer’s nucleotide metabolism — how tumors remodel their building blocks — emerged from multi-omics. plos-pone-0350854: Diabetic retinopathy — caught early, blindness prevented. This paper applied vision transformers to that early detection. The AI approach promises to screen the millions of diabetics at risk — catching retinal damage before vision is lost.
plos-pone-0353554: Rural tourism satisfaction — shaped by place and generation. This paper examined how those factors matter for resident satisfaction. The findings reveal the generational divides in how rural communities experience tourism — essential for development that doesn’t alienate its hosts.
plos-pone-0349654: Sheep ownership identification — by AI — for precision livestock farming. MSPFormer is an enhanced multi-scale, semantic-preserving transformer for the task. plos-pone-0353654: Knee osteoarthritis — treated with invasive laser acupuncture at 650 and 830 nm. This pilot randomized trial tested efficacy and safety. plos-pone-0354254: Bridge cracks — detected by YOLO11-FR with frequency-domain fusion and edge enhancement. This paper built it. The detector found fractures invisible to standard vision. The findings automated the watch over aging bridges — AI as the infrastructure inspector.
plos-pone-0353354: Salvia miltiorrhiza exosome-like nanoparticles — their miRNAs functionally analyzed for gastric cancer treatment. This paper characterized them. The findings revealed plant vesicles carrying anti-tumor RNA. The research bridged traditional medicine and nanomedicine — danshen’s nanoparticles against stomach cancer.
plos-pone-0353954: Cisplatin — the chemotherapy mainstay — destroys hearing, and mouse models help us understand how. The ultrasonic approach probed hearing beyond the conventional range. The findings validated a sensitive assay — detecting ototoxic damage earlier and more precisely than standard methods allow.
plos-pone-0352654: Soft grippers — designed with dielectric elastomer actuators on quadrangular star honeycomb supports. This paper researched that design. The bio-inspired structure grasped delicately yet firmly. The findings advanced soft robotics — machines handling the fragile with engineered grace.
plos-pone-0351254: Organizational dehumanization — a multidimensional scale developed and validated in higher education. This paper built it. The findings measured being treated as a tool. plos-pone-0353154: Flexible Stewart platform — forward and inverse kinematics modeled and analyzed. This paper did so. The findings tamed the parallel robot’s mathematics. plos-pone-0350554: Interprofessional collaboration — nine keys distilled from observing treatment meetings’ facilitators and barriers. This qualitative study did so. plos-pone-0352254: Breast cancer — cell-cell junction gene signatures as subtype-specific prognostic biomarkers. This paper identified them. plos-pone-0343954: Art style classification — a network integrating contrastive learning and counterfactual attention. This paper built it. The analysis taught the machine to see style. plos-pone-0351754: Evidence-based practice measure — cross-culturally adapted among Hong Kong healthcare providers. This paper did so. The analysis tuned the instrument to the territory. plos-pone-0352154: Amputation decisions — patient quality of life determinants. This paper studied them. The analysis asked what makes life worth the limb’s loss. plos-pone-0352454: Pulmonary adenosquamous carcinoma — comparative CT and pathological features versus adeno and squamous cell carcinomas. This paper did so. plos-pone-0351154: Selflessness and self-centeredness — adapted from traits to daily experiences with a day-level inventory. This paper built the adaptation. europmc-pmc2793254: Sorting out plant family trees gets hard at the level of closely related species. europmc-pmc2825554: A cell sheet in the eye does more than guard the blood-eye wall, this 2010 paper says. europmc-pmc2832754: A single gene, LRRK2, is the most common genetic cause of Parkinson's disease. europmc-pmc2838754: Knowing how cattle are related sharpens DNA-based breeding predictions. europmc-pmc2846954: Some risk factors matter more early and less later, complicating survival analysis. europmc-pmc2851054: Opioid drugs hijack the brain's own pain and reward circuits. This 2002 review lays out the brain science of opioid dependence and what it means for treatment. europmc-pmc2859054: Drusen, the yellow deposits in aging eyes, foreshadow macular degeneration. This 2010 paper catalogs their rich fat and protein contents. The authors' chemical census shows drusen are far from simple debris. Their data feeds theories of how age steals central vision.
europmc-pmc2905354: Myasthenia gravis saps muscle strength, and this 2010 review counts its toll. The authors pull together population studies of the disease across countries. Their synthesis maps who it strikes and how often. The review fills a gap for a rare disease.
europmc-pmc2923754: Asthma is not just twitchy airways; it is lasting inflammation. This 2010 review covers chronic inflammation and asthma, from immune cells to airway remodeling. europmc-pmc2935454: The Thanksgiving turkey got its genome read. europmc-pmc3021854: Cow burps warm the planet, and this 2010 review tackles them. The authors cover the gut germs that make the methane and how to curb them. Their overview guides feed science. The work aids climate goals. Seaweed feed cuts the burps sharply.

europmc-pmc6515654: Alzheimer's memory loss may be eased by tiny delivery vans: exosomes - nano-sized bubbles shed by stem cells - fitted with a brain-homing tag called RVG. europmc-pmc6529554: As antibiotics lose power, researchers are raiding the plant kingdom for replacements - and the Middle East's flora is rich hunting ground. europmc-pmc6591954: Oxford Nanopore sequencers read DNA by sensing electric current - but translating the squiggles into letters (basecalling) needs neural networks. europmc-pmc6642154: Th17 immune cells are villains in many inflammatory diseases - yet the gut needs its own peaceful Th17 residents to keep the barrier sound. europmc-pmc6650554: Candida auris - a drug-resistant yeast - appeared almost simultaneously on three continents, a medical mystery. europmc-pmc6678954: Osteoarthritis grinds joints down - and a master inflammation switch called NF-kB helps drive the wrecking. europmc-pmc6702654: Hydrogels - watery scaffolds for growing replacement tissue - tend to crack under strain. Self-healing versions stitch themselves back together, and this review asks whether they are tissue engineering's next big leap. Durable, self-repairing scaffolds could make lab-grown tissues far more practical.
europmc-pmc6728754: Monocytes - blood's versatile immune cells - come in three flavors: classical, intermediate, and non-classical. This review profiles each subset's markers and jobs across major chronic inflammatory diseases. Knowing which monocyte does what clarifies their roles in conditions from arthritis to atherosclerosis.
europmc-pmc6776654: Gut microbes are chemical factories - and their products enter our blood. Using whole-metagenome data, this study mapped how the microbiome's metabolic output intertwines with human metabolism. The interplay reveals the gut as a second liver, shaping health from the inside.
europmc-pmc6796854: An Alzheimer's drug derived from seaweed remodels the gut - and the brain benefits. Sodium oligomannate reshapes gut bacteria and their amino-acid output, calming the microbial signals tied to Alzheimer's. The gut-brain axis gets a therapeutic foothold.
europmc-pmc6799954: Drinking problems and depression travel together - far too often. This review untangles their co-occurrence: how common the pairing is, how it unfolds, and what treatments help both. The dual diagnosis demands dual attention.
europmc-pmc6801754: One test is rarely enough to read a disease - precision medicine needs a chorus. This paper argues for multi-omics marker patterns: combining gene, protein, and chemical clues into medical panels. The layered approach could at last match drugs to people. Many small hints beat one loud one.
europmc-pmc6892854: Stomach growths hire local stem cells as aides. This study shows stomach cancer-derived local support cells flip guard cells to the M2 switch that fuels spread. The support crew are drug marks. Cut the hiring, stall the spread. The tumor support crew makes a prime target.
europmc-pmc6974454: Mouth bugs may push oral cancer along. This review weighs whether the mouth bugs sway oral cancer: the mouth-cancer link. The germ suspects. Long flare-ups is the probable link. gao-gaoreports-gao-08-54: Millions in bad contract payouts — that's what GAO found at the agency that runs Medicare and Medicaid in this 2007 report. gao-gaoreports-gao-06-854: The visa waiver program needed a risk check in 2006, and GAO's report says stronger actions were required to assess and mitigate the dangers. The findings demand the scrutiny. The report warns that the open door needed a better lock. The risks had to be managed.
gao-gaoreports-gao-06-554: Highway tolling was spreading in 2006, and GAO's report says states' expanding use illustrated diverse challenges and strategies. The findings map the trend. The report warns that the pay-to-drive wave needed honest accounting. The strategies had to be weighed.
gao-gaoreports-gao-06-654: Medicare drug benefit letters needed clarity in 2006, and GAO's report says communications to beneficiaries could improve. The findings demand the plain talk. gao-gaoreports-gao-06-454: The Army Corps' Mississippi classroom contract got a GAO look in 2006, and the report examines the Katrina-related deal. The findings review the procurement. The report warns that the storm's schoolrooms deserved honest bidding. The contract had to be sound.

gao-gaoreports-gao-06-154: The national airspace transformation needed cultural change in 2005, and GAO's report says the overhaul required new thinking and balanced funding. The findings prescribe the shift. The report warns that the crowded skies deserved modern control. The change had to come.
openalex-w7204102154: Bleeding inside the brain needs surgery, but how much cutting is best? This review pits small-hole techniques against opening the skull for sudden brain bleeds. openalex-w7160150454: Chilled near absolute zero, a samarium compound lines up its magnetism in a strange pattern. A deep-freeze physics study of magnetism's strangest layouts.
openalex-w7133323154: Irregular heartbeats can hide in young, healthy-seeming adults. This study screened 403 adults aged 18 to 40 with questionnaires to spot silent atrial fibrillation. openalex-w7204804154: Wasting muscles signal trouble in advanced cancer. arxiv-2606-15954: As AI agents grow more complex, they cost more money and energy to run. Green SARC is a framework that predicts and manages both the financial cost and the carbon footprint of agentic AI systems together. The paper offers organizations a way to govern their AI spending and environmental impact before either one runs out of control.
arxiv-2606-16454: LoRA fine-tunes big models with small updates, but its gradients can scale unevenly across directions — "anisotropic gradient scaling" — slowing learning. arxiv-2606-16554: A pure mathematics paper on discrete Laplacians — the graph version of the operator governing heat flow and vibrations — in the m-sectorial setting, with complex-valued weights.
